entries.description: bulletproof-react Vite app (createBrowserRouter data router, MSW mocks)
entries.install: cd apps/react-vite && yarn install && cp -n .env.example .env; true
entries.notes: Routes are `lazy: () => import(...).then(convert)`; the static side awaits the import and materializes the module namespace through `convert`'s rest spread. QueryClientProvider, HelmetProvider, react-error-boundary and react-query-auth's AuthLoader are opaque with slotted children; Helmet's <meta> is a side effect, not a fiber, so that slot stays unmatched.

entries.description: Epic Stack (React Router framework mode, file-convention routes via react-router-auto-routes, Prisma)
entries.notes: routes.ts delegates to react-router-auto-routes; the static side mirrors its file conventions (_layout nesting, pathless _groups, $params, [.] escapes, trailing-underscore opt-outs) to rebuild the route table without running the generator. Loader data, honeypot and theme values stay unknown. @radix-ui, remix-utils, openimg, sonner and spin-delay are analyzed from source (each would otherwise leave opaque fibers or a branch); @conform-to, @epic-web and @nasa-gcn/remix-seo analyze cleanly but change no fiber, so they stay external.

entries.description: Sentry frontend login page (React 19 SPA on react-router data routers, rspack dev server in UI-only mode proxying the API to sentry.io)
entries.dev: bash "$BIPPY_CORPUS_SCRIPTS/with-node.sh" 24 npx -y pnpm@10.30.2 exec rspack serve
entries.notes: index.tsx boots asynchronously: in SaaS mode it registers the getsentry overrides, loads the /api/client-config/ payload (window.__initialData, captured from the live page) into ConfigStore and then calls renderDom(Main), so the static side runs the same bootstrap before rendering the exported Main component. UI-only mode serves the SPA over a self-signed https certificate; the login page fetches from sentry.io and logs 403s for unauthenticated endpoints.

entries.description: PostHog login scene (React 18 SPA on kea + kea-router, Vite dev server behind a stand-in for the Django app server that renders the boot HTML)
entries.notes: Django normally renders index.html with window.POSTHOG_APP_CONTEXT and points the module scripts at the Vite dev server; corpus/scripts/posthog-app-server.ts stands in for it with an anonymous app context and the checked-in _preflight fixture, answering the API calls the login scene makes. The kea store the page builds is captured through the Redux DevTools compose hook and replayed into the static render; the app server's stand-in API returns 404 for the endpoints it does not model, which the page logs.

entries.notes: The setup script writes the repository `.env` (SQLite `DATA_DIR`, NextAuth secret) and symlinks it into `apps/web` so `next dev` loads it; `pnpm db:migrate` creates the database. `/` redirects unauthenticated visitors to `/signin`, which is captured directly. The background workers, Meilisearch and the headless Chrome container are not started (not needed for the sign-in page). Runs on Node 22 rather than the repository's `.nvmrc` 24: `better-sqlite3@11.3.0` has no Node 24 prebuild and its locally compiled binary aborts `next-server` (`RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` assertion) when Next tears down a worker.

entries.description: Plane web app sign-in page (React Router framework mode with ssr: false, pnpm + Turborepo monorepo, Django API from the repository's Docker development stack)
entries.notes: `plane-services.sh` copies the three `.env.example` files and brings up `docker-compose-local.yml` (PostgreSQL, Valkey, RabbitMQ, MinIO, migrator, API on :8000) with `plane-compose.override.yml`, which unpublishes the database/cache host ports so they cannot collide with the other corpus containers. `turbo run dev --filter=web` builds the workspace packages first (they export `dist/`), then runs `react-router dev --port 3000`. `plane-setup.sh` symlinks `@tailwindcss/postcss` (a dependency of `packages/tailwind-config` only) into `apps/web/node_modules` because `apps/web/postcss.config.js` re-exports the shared config and postcss-load-config resolves plugin names from `apps/web`. Run with `--corpus-dir` outside this monorepo: `@react-router/dev` pre-bundles `react-router-dom` whenever `require.resolve` finds one from the app root, and a checkout nested under bippy picks up bippy's unrelated `react-router-dom@6`, which fails esbuild's optimizer against `react-router@7`.

entries.description: Twenty CRM front sign-in page (Vite SPA with Jotai + Apollo, Yarn 4 + Nx monorepo, NestJS server over local PostgreSQL + Redis containers)
entries.dev: bash "$BIPPY_CORPUS_SCRIPTS/with-node.sh" 24 env -u FORCE_COLOR npx nx run-many -t start -p twenty-server twenty-front
entries.notes: The setup script copies both `.env.example` files, points the server at the corpus PostgreSQL/Redis containers and runs `nx run twenty-server:database:init` (builds the server, creates the schema, applies instance migrations). `nx run-many -t start` runs the NestJS server (:3000) and the Vite dev server (:3001) together; the worker is not started. `twenty-shared` (a workspace package the front resolves through its built `dist/`) holds the `AppPath` route constants; `twenty-ui` is not analyzed because materializing its subtree overflows the stack / heap (see results residuals).

entries.description: Langfuse web sign-in page (Next pages router, pnpm + Turborepo monorepo, Prisma over the repository's Docker development stack)

The setup script copies `.env.dev.example` to `.env` (telemetry disabled), generates the Prisma client, builds `@langfuse/shared` (the web app resolves its `dist/`) and applies the Prisma migrations; the ClickHouse migrations are not applied (they need the golang-migrate CLI and the sign-in page does not query ClickHouse).

entries.description: Glide Data Grid next-gdg test project (Next 12 pages router, React 17)
entries.install: npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build -w packages/core
entries.notes: The project's package-lock pins the published @glideapps/glide-data-grid@3.4.1, which no longer exports the dist/index.css _app.tsx imports, so like test-projects/bootstrap-projects.sh the setup symlinks the built packages/core into node_modules (`--legacy-peer-deps`: the lock pairs marked@16 with a marked@^4 peer range) and additionally aliases react/react-dom in next.config.js to the project's React 17 so core's dist does not load the repository root's React 19. The static side aliases the package to packages/core/src so both trees come from the same revision.

entries.description: Material React Table docs site home page (Next 14 pages router, React 19, MUI)
entries.notes: The docs app consumes the workspace package's dist build, whose rollup config uses `assert { type: 'json' }` import assertions that Node 22 rejects, so the library is built under Node 20. Next 14 externalizes the pnpm-hoisted @mui/* server modules as ESM and Node rejects their directory subpath imports (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT on @mui/utils/formatMuiErrorMessage), so setup turns off experimental.esmExternals in next.config.js; the static side aliases material-react-table to packages/material-react-table/src.
